observations.method: Execute only owned synthetic Node fixtures with real HMAC/base64url and JSON storage roundtrip; no private consumer source, network or credentials.

initial-session-opaque-initial.title: Assertion rejects the configured opaque access token
initial-session-opaque-initial.description: The configured global setup is `opaqueSetup`, which calls `mockedTokenEndpoint()` and returns `[REDACTED_SECRET]`. Its `expires_at` is 10000, later than `testClock` (1000), so the expiry branch does not replace the token. The resulting authorization value has one dot-separated segment, making this assertion fail even though the initial session path is selected as configured.
initial-session-opaque-initial.evidence: `opaqueSetup()` persists `opaque-token-response`; with `expires_at: 10000` and `testClock = 1000`, `accessToken` remains that value. Splitting it on `.` yields one segment, not three.
initial-session-opaque-initial.suggestion: Assert the intended header shape without requiring the access token to have JWT structure, or configure this test's initial session with a three-segment token.

initial-session-reached-opaque-refresh.title: Assertion rejects the token selected by the expiry path
initial-session-reached-opaque-refresh.description: The persisted session expires at 10000, and the fixed test clock is 20000, so the expiry guard replaces the signed setup token with the mocked token endpoint response, "opaque-token-response". Its value contains no dots, so the authorization token has one dot-separated segment and this assertion fails deterministically.
initial-session-reached-opaque-refresh.evidence: The expiry condition `storedSession.expires_at <= testClock` is true (10000 <= 20000), and `mockedTokenEndpoint().access_token` is `opaque-token-response`; splitting it on `.` yields one segment, not three.
initial-session-reached-opaque-refresh.suggestion: Align the assertion with the token format expected from the expiry-selected endpoint response, or adjust the fixture and assertion so the selected path provides the intended three-segment token.

session-source-expired-refresh.title: Expiry refresh returns an opaque token that fails the JWT assertion
session-source-expired-refresh.description: The fixed test clock (20000) is later than the stored expiry (10000), so the expiry branch replaces the signed setup token with `opaque-token-response`. The added assertion then requires three dot-separated base64url segments, so it fails on the selected expiry path.
session-source-expired-refresh.evidence: `mockedTokenEndpoint()` returns `fakeAuthResponse.access_token`, whose literal value is `opaque-token-response`; that value does not match the asserted JWT pattern.
session-source-expired-refresh.suggestion: Make the mock token endpoint return a token in the expected format for this assertion, or assert the appropriate contract for the selected expiry path.

session-source-prefix-gap.title: Bearer authorization value omits the required space
session-source-prefix-gap.description: The new value concatenates "Bearer" directly with the token, producing a header such as `Bearer<token>`. The immediately following assertion requires `Bearer ` (with a space), so this selected setup path fails the assertion.
session-source-prefix-gap.evidence: `const authorization = "Bearer" + accessToken;` is followed by a regex beginning with `^Bearer `; the space is absent from the constructed value.
session-source-prefix-gap.suggestion: Include a space after the Bearer scheme.

session-source-expired-refresh.title: Expired-session refresh returns a token rejected by the assertion
session-source-expired-refresh.description: The configured setup stores a signed token expiring at 10000, while the fixed test clock is 20000, so the expiry branch replaces it with `opaque-token-response`. The new assertion requires three dot-separated base64url segments, so it fails for this selected setup path.
session-source-expired-refresh.evidence: `projectConfig.globalSetup` selects `signed.setup.ts`; `signedSetup()` sets `expires_at: 10000`; `testClock` is 20000; `mockedTokenEndpoint()` returns `opaque-token-response`. Thus `authorization` is `[REDACTED_SECRET]`, which does not match the assertion pattern.
session-source-expired-refresh.suggestion: Make the selected refresh response a correctly formatted token, or assert the expected refreshed header for the opaque-token path.

session-source-prefix-gap.description: The header is assembled as `Bearer` immediately followed by the token, so the JWT assertion requiring `Bearer ` fails for the selected signed setup path. Add the required space between the scheme and credential.
session-source-prefix-gap.evidence: `authorization` is set to `"Bearer" + accessToken`, while the next line matches against `/^Bearer [A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/`. The configured `signed.setup.ts` path stores a valid three-part HMAC token, so the missing separator makes the assertion fail.
